differences.what: Massing: three storeys over a raised basement at the photograph's heights (principal floor 1.65 m, the projection's top 9.45 m, the wall head 12.45 m) — the draft's were the rules' (T-2543)

Gable: the front carried up as a shaped Flemish gable over the whole front, swelling from a kneeler each side and drawn in to a pointed head under a finial at 17.0-17.5 m, in place of the draft's stepped boxes (T-2543)
Gable: the outline's swell still stands 10-20 px wide of the print's below the shoulders, and its shoulder stones are not built as blocks
Gable: the grid window is nine lights (three by three) between stone mullions and transoms; K06's attic group builds three tall lights
Gable: its face is the wall's own plane in the photograph; here it stands 0.5 m proud of the wall below on a square base, so the hip's eave dies into it
Gable: the kneelers are carved scrolls under small pinnacles; built as plain square pinnacles
South projection: carried through the basement and two storeys to a flat top at the third floor, with the round-arched window, the basement light and the paired window in it (T-2543)
South projection: flush with the south corner in the photograph; K08 stands it 0.3 m in
South projection: the barred basement light stands from about 0.1 m over the walk and is about 1 m high; K08 keeps it clear of the 0.6 m plinth, 0.65 m high
Balcony: the iron balcony on the projection's top
Third storey: the large round-arched window with its fanlight over the balcony and the smaller arched window to its north, with their voussoirs; built flat-headed and smaller
Second storey: the north pair is one wide window (1.66 m) under a transom; built as K01's widest single sash (1.15 m)
Entrance: the porch's broad round arch (about 3.2 m across, its crown at about 5.2 m) over the door and its side light; built as K07's deep-arched double door
Stair: a straight stair to the walk between solid stone balustrades with a pierced panel at the landing; K07's stoop has plain cheeks
Fabric: rock-faced stone basement and a stone first storey under brick upper storeys banded and dressed in stone, the carved frieze and bosses; the whole street front is built in stone
Downpipes down both ends of the front
Roof: the steep slated slopes the photograph shows behind the gable's shoulders, flat-topped like a mansard's; built as K01's hip (T-2545)
Colour: the print is monochrome, so every stone, brick and paint colour
The side and rear walls, which the photograph does not see
